learningObjective: Distinguish constant folding from constant propagation and identify when folding is legal.
irSnippet:
; Before folding
%a = add i32 3, 4
%b = mul i32 %a, 2
%c = add i32 %b, 5

; After constant folding
%c = i32 19
stem: Constant folding transforms the IR shown above by evaluating arithmetic on compile-time constants. Which statement about constant folding is correct?

options.text: Constant folding evaluates operations whose operands are all compile-time constants at compile time, producing a new constant. It must respect the source semantics for overflow, rounding, and floating-point edge cases (NaN, infinity) — otherwise it can change program behavior.
Constant folding requires SSA form; a non-SSA IR cannot support folding because reaching definitions are ambiguous.
Constant folding is identical to constant propagation; both refer to substituting known values into use sites.
Constant folding may reorder floating-point operations freely because IEEE-754 arithmetic is associative.

explanation: Constant folding computes constant expressions at compile time but must preserve semantics — integer overflow behavior, floating-point rounding, NaN/Inf handling. Constant propagation is a distinct (but related) optimization: it replaces variable uses with their known constant values. Non-SSA IRs can also fold; SSA simplifies but is not required. IEEE-754 floating-point is NOT associative, so reordering is not always safe.

optionExplanations.A: Correct: standard definition with the important semantic-preservation caveats.
optionExplanations.B: Wrong: constant folding is applicable in both SSA and non-SSA IRs.
optionExplanations.C: Wrong: folding evaluates operations; propagation replaces uses. They are related but distinct.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: IEEE-754 addition/multiplication are NOT associative; naive reordering may change results (see -ffast-math implications).

assumptions: IR represents integer and/or floating-point operations with well-defined semantics.
nonImplications: Does not imply all constant expressions are folded; e.g., division by zero may need to be preserved as a trap.
Does not imply folding is 'free' compile-time work; large expressions may increase compile time.
